title: Pointwise CATE Risk Frontier under a Rough Bounded-Positive Covariate Density
banked_reason: The numerical phase itself largely coincides with the published KBRW phase; the projected paper-score ceiling 7.3 is below the field floor 7.4.
gap_reasons: The numerical phase itself largely coincides with the published KBRW phase
The interval result is only a conservative Markov conversion of the MSE bound with known smoothness parameters and very large constants

The one-dimensional, equal-nuisance-smoothness, fixed-interior-point setting and absence of numerical evidence showing when the close-pair estimator improves on existing procedures constrain the leading-journal case
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a matched one-dimensional pointwise minimax phase on the bounded-positive-density class, including a density-free close-pair estimator, a full-support lower construction, and conservative honest intervals. Primary-source citation checks and the maximality audit passed with no open discovery statements. D0.5 capped novelty at subfield below the fixed field floor, so formal Lean translation was not attempted; a field-tier follow-on needs a substantive new scope or inference result.
tldr: For every \(s,\gamma\in(0,1]\), the exact pointwise absolute-risk frontier for the continuous observed-law contrast \(\tau_P(x_0)\) over the bounded-positive-density class is \(\psi_n(s,\gamma)\): below the elbow \(s=\gamma/\{2(2\gamma+1)\}\) its exponent is \(\{1+1/(2\gamma)+1/(4s)\}^{-1}\), and at or above the elbow it is \(\gamma/(2\gamma+1)\). The explicit thresholded close-pair ratio attains this rate without estimating the covariate density, and full-support binary-outcome subfamilies give the matching converse. Deterministic clipped intervals centered at the tuned estimator have uniform coverage at least \(1-\eta\) and expected length \(O\{\psi_n(s,\gamma)/\sqrt\eta\}\). The original \(s=1/10\), \(\gamma=1\) rate \(n^{-1/4}\) and its interval are fixed-slice corollaries. Consistency and conditional exchangeability supply only the stated \(P_X\)-almost-sure causal interpretation.
gap: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman derive the relevant low-smoothness exponent, but their upper theorem retains a covariate-distribution remainder and their displayed lower construction does not certify the converse inside the everywhere-positive-density subclass.
fill: The project pairs an explicit finite close-pair ratio with a full-support binary fuzzy-hypothesis construction, yielding upper and lower bounds on one class and exposing honest rate-optimal inference as the first open rung.
